name: Pioglitazone
summary: An insulin-sensitizing PPAR-gamma agonist used in type 2 diabetes, notable for durable glycemic control but fluid-retention risk.
mechanism: Activates the nuclear receptor PPAR-gamma, altering adipocyte, muscle, and hepatic gene expression to improve insulin sensitivity and reduce hepatic glucose output.
pharmacodynamics: Lowers insulin resistance and A1c durably; reduces triglycerides and redistributes fat to subcutaneous depots.

dosing.adult: 15–30 mg once daily; may increase to 45 mg once daily

safety.pregnancy: Not recommended; insulin is standard during pregnancy
contraindications: Active liver disease or ALT >2.5× ULN
warnings: Fluid retention and edema, risk of new or worsening heart failure
Possible increased fracture risk in women
monitoring: Signs of edema or heart failure
safety.overdose: Hypoglycemia is unlikely alone; supportive care

indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, alone or in combination
Type 2 diabetes with significant insulin resistance or NAFLD where other agents are unsuitable
clinicalPearls: Full glycemic effect takes weeks — do not judge efficacy early.
Fluid retention is markedly worse when combined with insulin; watch for heart failure symptoms.
good: Durable insulin sensitizer useful in insulin-resistant phenotypes, with a favorable lipid profile.
bad: Heart failure, significant edema, or patients where weight gain is unacceptable.
